intro: A LocalNodes site is one home for a community, with groups inside it. These are some of the kinds of community it fits, and what each would do in its first week.
closing: A single group with no network is welcome too.

kinds.heading: Housing co-ops
kinds.who: Your co-op has several houses and plenty to remember.
kinds.shape: The co-op has one site, with each house as a group.
firstWeek: Add the minutes and repair log.
Ask about the back steps and open the cited page.

kinds.heading: Markets and local business groups
kinds.who: Vendors and shopkeepers keep local trade moving.
kinds.shape: A market or business association has one site, with vendors or shops as groups.
firstWeek: Add a page showing who sets up where.
Post the next market day or evening market on the calendar.

kinds.heading: Neighborhood associations
kinds.who: Members get things done between meetings.
kinds.shape: An association has one site, with groups for its blocks or committees.
firstWeek: Put the garden day on the calendar.
Run a quick poll: Saturday morning or Sunday afternoon?

kinds.heading: Makerspaces and shared studios
kinds.who: Makers and studio members swap tips across town.
kinds.shape: The town's spaces share one site, with a group for each space.
firstWeek: Post the next open house on the calendar.
Save the kiln notes before the person who knows them goes away.

kinds.heading: Community-run gatherings, conferences and unconferences
kinds.who: You're planning a gathering or unconference together.
kinds.shape: The gathering has one site, with tracks, working groups or session hosts as groups.
firstWeek: Add the schedule and session notes; ask which sessions cover food growing and open the source.
Decide the program together, with every organizer who has a say. Pay session grants from the group fund.

kinds.heading: Tenant unions
kinds.who: Tenants share notes and organize across several buildings.
kinds.shape: One union site brings them together, with a group for each building.
firstWeek: Collect the meeting notes and repair letters.
Ask which repairs the notes mention and check the cited passage.

kinds.heading: Community gardens
kinds.who: Gardeners share space, tools and know-how.
kinds.shape: One garden has a site, with plots or work crews as groups.
firstWeek: Put the shed cleanup on the calendar.
Keep watering notes where the next pair of hands can find them.

kinds.heading: Outdoor clubs, climbing clubs and sports leagues
kinds.who: You're planning a climb, a muddy hike or the next match.
kinds.shape: A club or league has one site, with groups for its teams.
firstWeek: Add the next outing or match to the calendar.
Share the gear list before someone forgets the cooler.

kinds.heading: Arts collectives
kinds.who: Artists make things together, sometimes in different rooms.
kinds.shape: One collective has a site, with groups for projects or working teams.
firstWeek: Post the open-studio date on the calendar.
Save the hanging plan and installation notes in the group's library.

kinds.heading: Parent-teacher groups, congregations and student organizations
kinds.who: You're planning the fundraiser, potluck or next semester's event.
kinds.shape: Each organization has a site, with committees or clubs as groups.
firstWeek: Ask which event dates work in a quick poll.
Keep the handover notes for next year's volunteers.

kinds.heading: Tool libraries, food co-ops and mutual aid networks
kinds.who: Members share tools, organize food and help one another.
kinds.shape: One network has a site, with groups for branches or volunteer teams.
firstWeek: Put pick-up days and volunteer meetups on the calendar.
Collect the handover notes so new volunteers can get their bearings.
